learn.hook: Why do people in Himachal Pradesh build their fields like giant staircases? Because they live on mountains!
points: A mountain is land that rises high above its surroundings, with steep slopes and often a pointed top called a peak.
A long chain of mountains is called a range. The Himalayas, to the north of India, are the highest mountain range in the world.
Mount Everest, in the Himalayas, is the highest peak in the world. Other ranges in India include the Aravalli and the Western Ghats.
High mountains have glaciers, which are slow-moving rivers of ice. Many rivers begin from them; the Ganga starts from the Gangotri glacier.
Life in the mountains: cold weather, thin air and steep land. People grow crops on terraces (step fields), keep animals like yaks and sheep, and many earn from tourism.

example.q: Why do farmers in the mountains cut their fields into steps (terraces)?
steps: Mountain slopes are steep.
On a steep slope, rainwater rushes down and washes away soil and seeds.
Flat steps slow the water and hold the soil, so crops can grow.
example.answer: Terraces make flat land on slopes and stop soil from being washed away.

learn.reallife: Tea gardens in Darjeeling, apple orchards in Himachal Pradesh and yak herders in Ladakh are all part of mountain life in India.

games.title: Mountain facts
items: The Himalayas are the highest mountain range in the world.
They have the world's tallest peaks, including Mount Everest.
A glacier is a slow-moving river of ice.
Glaciers form from snow piling up over many years.
The Ganga begins from the Gangotri glacier.
The Ganga starts as the Bhagirathi from the Gangotri glacier in Uttarakhand.
Air on high mountains has more oxygen than air at sea level.
The air gets thinner higher up, so there is less oxygen to breathe.
Terrace farming is done on flat plains.
Terraces are cut on hill and mountain slopes.

games.title: Mountain words
pairs: the pointed top of a mountain
a step-like field on a slope
a hairy animal reared in high, cold places

quiz.q: Which is the highest mountain range in the world?
quiz.explain: The Himalayas, to India's north, have the highest peaks on Earth.
steps: A range is a long chain of mountains.
The Himalayas, north of India, are the highest range in the world.
The Aravalli and Western Ghats are lower Indian ranges. Answer: The Himalayas
quiz.mistake: Picks another mountain range without comparing heights

quiz.q: Which is the highest mountain peak in the world?
quiz.explain: Mount Everest, in the Himalayas, is the highest peak in the world.
steps: The highest peak lies in the highest range, the Himalayas.
That peak is Mount Everest.
Answer: Mount Everest
quiz.mistake: Confuses a hill station or another peak with Everest

quiz.q: What is a glacier?
quiz.explain: Glaciers are huge masses of ice that slide slowly down valleys.
steps: High mountains have glaciers.
A glacier is a slow-moving river (mass) of ice.
Answer: A slow-moving mass of ice
quiz.mistake: Thinks a glacier is a kind of waterfall

quiz.q: From which glacier does the Ganga begin?
quiz.explain: The Ganga begins as the Bhagirathi at the Gangotri glacier in Uttarakhand.
steps: Many rivers begin from glaciers.
The Ganga starts from the Gangotri glacier.
Answer: Gangotri
quiz.mistake: Picks another Himalayan glacier

quiz.q: Why is it harder to breathe on very high mountains?
options: The air is thinner, with less oxygen
The air is full of water
quiz.explain: Higher up, air is thin, so each breath has less oxygen.
steps: Mountain life: cold, thin air and steep land.
Thin air has less oxygen in each breath.
So breathing is harder. It is cold, not hot, up there.
Answer: The air is thinner, with less oxygen
quiz.mistake: Thinks high places are hot and stuffy

quiz.q: What is terrace farming?
options: Growing crops on step-like fields cut into slopes
quiz.explain: Terraces turn steep slopes into small flat steps that hold soil and water.
steps: Mountain slopes are steep.
Farmers cut slopes into steps (terraces) to make flat land.
Terraces also stop soil being washed away.
Answer: Growing crops on step-like fields cut into slopes
quiz.mistake: Takes 'terrace' to mean the roof of a house

quiz.q: Which animal is reared by herders in the cold, high Himalayas such as Ladakh?
quiz.explain: Yaks have thick hair that keeps them warm in high, cold places.
steps: The high Himalayas are very cold.
Herders there keep yaks (and sheep).
Yaks' thick hair keeps them warm. Camels suit deserts. Answer: Yak
quiz.mistake: Picks an animal suited to deserts or plains

quiz.q: Why are mountain areas usually less crowded than plains?
options: Mountains have no water at all
Steep slopes, cold weather and little flat land make life harder
quiz.explain: It is difficult to farm, build and travel on steep, cold slopes, so fewer people live there.
steps: Mountains have cold weather, thin air and steep land.
Farming, building and travel are hard there.
So fewer people live there than on plains.
Answer: Steep slopes, cold weather and little flat land make life harder
quiz.mistake: Thinks mountains are empty for a rule-based reason

teach.ask: Gappu is planning a trip to Ladakh. 'What will mountains be like? How do people live there?'
teach.praise: Brrr! Mountains are high and cold with glaciers, and people farm on step-like terraces. I'll pack a sweater!
teach.nudge: What is the weather like up there, and how do people farm on steep slopes?

revise.summary: Mountains rise high above their surroundings with steep slopes and peaks; a chain of them is a range. The Himalayas are the highest range, Everest the highest peak, and mountain life means cold, thin air and steep land.
focus: Mountain, peak and range; the Himalayas and Mount Everest
Other Indian ranges: Aravalli and Western Ghats
Glaciers as slow rivers of ice; the Ganga starts from Gangotri
Mountain life: terraces, yaks and sheep, tourism, thin air
remember: Highest range: the Himalayas; highest peak: Mount Everest
Ganga begins at the Gangotri glacier
Terraces = step fields that make flat land and save soil
traps: Don't confuse a range (chain of mountains) with a peak (one top)
It is harder to breathe high up because the air is thin, not because it is hot
Yaks belong to cold mountains; camels belong to deserts

learn.hook: Imagine a giant table made of rock: high up, but flat on top. That's a plateau!
points: A plateau is a raised area of land with a fairly flat top and steep sides. It is often called a tableland.
The Deccan Plateau covers a large part of southern India. The Chota Nagpur Plateau lies mainly in Jharkhand.
The Tibetan Plateau, north of the Himalayas, is the highest plateau in the world.
Many plateaus are rich in minerals. The Chota Nagpur Plateau has large amounts of coal and iron ore.
Rivers flowing off the edges of plateaus often form beautiful waterfalls, and the black soil of parts of the Deccan is good for growing cotton.

example.q: Why do many mines and steel plants come up in the Chota Nagpur Plateau?
steps: Steel is made from iron ore, and coal is used to heat the furnaces.
The Chota Nagpur Plateau has large amounts of both iron ore and coal.
Factories save money and time when the raw materials are nearby.
example.answer: Because the plateau is rich in coal and iron ore.

learn.reallife: Cities like Ranchi in Jharkhand and Pune and Bengaluru on the Deccan Plateau are built on plateaus.

games.title: Plateau or plain?
items: Raised land with a flat top and steep sides
Low, flat land made by rivers
Often called a tableland
Deccan
Land along the Ganga in Bihar
Rich in coal and iron ore in Jharkhand
Very fertile soil brought by rivers
Chota Nagpur

items.text: A plateau is also called a ___.
The ___ Plateau is the highest in the world.
The Chota Nagpur Plateau is rich in coal and ___.
The ___ Plateau covers much of southern India.

quiz.q: What is a plateau?
options: Raised land with a fairly flat top
A low land beside a river
quiz.explain: A plateau rises above the land around it but is flat on top, like a table.
steps: Fact: a plateau is raised land with a fairly flat top and steep sides.
A chain of mountains is a range; low flat land is a plain.
Answer: Raised land with a fairly flat top
quiz.mistake: Confuses a plateau with a mountain range

quiz.q: Why is a plateau often called a tableland?
options: It is high with a flat top, like a table
It has many tables of rock
quiz.explain: Its flat top and steep sides make it look like a table.
steps: A plateau is high with a flat top and steep sides.
That looks like a table.
So it is called a tableland.
Answer: It is high with a flat top, like a table
quiz.mistake: Takes the word 'tableland' too literally

quiz.q: Which is the highest plateau in the world?
quiz.explain: The Tibetan Plateau, north of the Himalayas, is the highest plateau on Earth.
steps: The Tibetan Plateau lies north of the Himalayas.
It is the highest plateau in the world.
The Deccan is large but not the highest. Answer: Tibetan Plateau
quiz.mistake: Picks the Deccan because it is the most famous in India

quiz.q: Which plateau covers a large part of southern India?
quiz.explain: The Deccan Plateau stretches across much of peninsular (southern) India.
steps: The Deccan Plateau covers a large part of southern India.
Chota Nagpur is mainly in Jharkhand; Tibetan is north of the Himalayas.
Answer: Deccan Plateau
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the plateaus of India

quiz.q: The Chota Nagpur Plateau is famous for which resources?
quiz.explain: This plateau in Jharkhand has rich deposits of coal, iron ore and other minerals.
steps: Many plateaus are rich in minerals.
Chota Nagpur has large amounts of coal and iron ore.
Answer: Coal and iron ore
quiz.mistake: Links plateaus with plantation crops instead of minerals

quiz.q: Why are waterfalls common on the edges of plateaus?
options: Rivers drop down the steep sides of the plateau
quiz.explain: When a river reaches the steep edge of a plateau, it falls down, forming a waterfall.
steps: Plateaus have steep sides.
Rivers flowing off the edges drop down these sides.
That drop forms waterfalls.
Answer: Rivers drop down the steep sides of the plateau
quiz.mistake: Does not link waterfalls to steep edges

quiz.q: The black soil of the Deccan Plateau is especially good for growing which crop?
quiz.explain: Black soil holds moisture well and is famous for cotton farming.
steps: Parts of the Deccan have black soil.
Black soil is good for growing cotton.
Answer: Cotton
quiz.mistake: Links any crop with any soil

quiz.q: Which city is located on the Chota Nagpur Plateau?
quiz.explain: Ranchi, the capital of Jharkhand, lies on the Chota Nagpur Plateau.
steps: The Chota Nagpur Plateau lies mainly in Jharkhand.
Ranchi is the capital of Jharkhand, on this plateau.
Kolkata, Chennai and Mumbai are coastal cities. Answer: Ranchi
quiz.mistake: Picks a coastal city

teach.ask: Gappu hops onto a flat-topped hill. 'Is this a mountain? It feels like a table!'
teach.praise: Yay! A plateau is high land with a flat top, like a table, and many plateaus hide minerals like coal and iron ore!
teach.nudge: What is special about the top of a plateau? And what treasures lie under some plateaus?

revise.summary: A plateau is raised land with a fairly flat top and steep sides, also called a tableland. Plateaus like Chota Nagpur are rich in minerals, and rivers falling off their edges form waterfalls.
focus: Definition of a plateau and why it is called a tableland
Deccan, Chota Nagpur and Tibetan plateaus and where they are
Minerals on plateaus: coal and iron ore in Chota Nagpur
Waterfalls at plateau edges; black soil of the Deccan for cotton
remember: Plateau = raised land, flat top, steep sides (tableland)
Tibetan Plateau = highest plateau in the world
Deccan Plateau covers much of southern India
Chota Nagpur (mainly Jharkhand) = coal and iron ore
traps: Don't call the Deccan the highest plateau; the Tibetan Plateau is
A plateau has a flat top; a mountain has a peak
Black soil of the Deccan is known for cotton, not tea

topics.title: Plains and how landforms shape life

learn.hook: Why do so many people live along the Ganga? Because plains are great for farming and building!
points: Plains are large stretches of low, flat land. Most are made by rivers that spread fine, fertile soil called alluvium.
The Indo-Gangetic plain in northern India, formed by the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra and their tributaries, is one of the most fertile plains in the world.
Plains are good for farming, building houses and laying roads and railways, so they are usually crowded with people and cities.
Each landform shapes life: mountains give rivers, forests and tourism; plateaus give minerals; plains give food crops.
Deserts like the Thar in Rajasthan are dry, sandy lands where people keep camels, save rainwater and wear loose, light clothes.

example.q: Why are there more big cities in plains than in mountains?
steps: Plains are flat, so it is easy to build houses, roads and railways.
Their fertile soil grows plenty of food.
Rivers give water for drinking and farming, so many people settle there.
example.answer: Flat land, fertile soil and plenty of water make plains easy to live in.

learn.reallife: The wheat in your roti and the rice in your plate likely grew on the plains of Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar or West Bengal.

games.title: Landform and life
pairs: mines of coal and iron ore
wide fields of wheat and rice

games.title: Plains true or false
items: Plains are usually low, flat land.
Plains are wide, flat stretches of land.
Rivers bring fertile soil to many plains.
This soil is called alluvium.
Plains are usually less crowded than mountains.
Plains are usually crowded because life there is easier.
The Thar Desert is in Rajasthan.
Most of India's Thar Desert lies in western Rajasthan.
It is harder to build railways on plains than on mountains.
Flat land makes it easier to build railways and roads.

quiz.q: What are plains?
options: Large areas of low, flat land
quiz.explain: Plains are wide, flat and generally low-lying.
steps: Fact: plains are large stretches of low, flat land.
High flat-topped land is a plateau.
Answer: Large areas of low, flat land
quiz.mistake: Confuses plains with plateaus

quiz.q: How are most river plains formed?
options: Rivers spread fine soil over the land
quiz.explain: Rivers carry fine, fertile soil (alluvium) and leave it over wide areas, building plains.
steps: Most plains are made by rivers.
Rivers spread fine, fertile soil (alluvium) over the land.
Answer: Rivers spread fine soil over the land
quiz.mistake: Thinks plains are pushed up like mountains

quiz.q: What is the fine, fertile soil left by rivers called?
quiz.explain: Alluvial soil is brought by rivers and is very good for farming.
steps: Rivers leave fine, fertile soil.
This soil is called alluvium.
Lava comes from volcanoes. Answer: Alluvium
quiz.mistake: Does not know the name of river soil

quiz.q: Which plain in northern India is formed by the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra river systems?
quiz.explain: This huge, fertile plain stretches across northern India.
steps: The Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra form a huge northern plain.
It is called the Indo-Gangetic plain.
Answer: Indo-Gangetic plain
quiz.mistake: Picks a name from another landform

quiz.q: Why are plains usually crowded with people?
options: Farming, building and travel are easy there
They are high above sea level
quiz.explain: Flat land, fertile soil and water from rivers make plains good for living.
steps: Plains are good for farming, houses, roads and railways.
So many people and cities are found there.
Minerals are found mostly on plateaus.
Answer: Farming, building and travel are easy there
quiz.mistake: Links crowding with cold or height

quiz.q: Which landform is best known for minerals like coal and iron ore?
quiz.explain: Many plateaus, like the Chota Nagpur Plateau, are rich in minerals.
steps: Mountains give rivers and forests; plains give food crops.
Plateaus give minerals like coal and iron ore.
Answer: Plateaus
quiz.mistake: Mixes up what each landform is known for

quiz.q: Which animal is most useful for travel in the Thar Desert?
quiz.explain: Camels can go long without water and walk easily on sand.
steps: The Thar is a dry, sandy desert.
People there keep camels for travel.
Yaks suit cold mountains. Answer: Camel
quiz.mistake: Picks an animal from mountains or cold regions

quiz.q: Which of these best shows how a landform shapes life?
options: People in the Thar grow rice in flooded fields
Yaks are herded on the hot plains of Bihar
Fishermen catch fish in the sands of the Thar
Farmers on plains grow lots of wheat and rice
quiz.explain: Plains have fertile soil and water, so they are India's main food-growing areas.
steps: Plains give food crops because of fertile soil and water.
So farmers on plains grow lots of wheat and rice.
The other options mismatch the land: no flooded rice in the dry Thar, no yaks on hot plains.
Answer: Farmers on plains grow lots of wheat and rice
quiz.mistake: Does not match the activity to the right landform

teach.ask: Gappu asks, 'Why do some people live in snowy mountains, some on rocky plateaus and so many on flat plains?'
teach.praise: Now I see! Plains are flat with fertile soil from rivers, so lots of people farm and live there. Each landform shapes how people live!
teach.nudge: Why do plains have such good soil, and why do so many people choose to live there?

revise.summary: Plains are large, low, flat lands mostly built by rivers that spread fertile alluvium. They are crowded because farming, building and travel are easy, and every landform shapes how people live.
focus: What plains are and how rivers form them with alluvium
The Indo-Gangetic plain and its rivers
Why plains are crowded with people and cities
How mountains, plateaus, plains and deserts each shape life
remember: Alluvium = fine, fertile soil left by rivers
Indo-Gangetic plain: Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra and tributaries
Mountains give rivers, forests, tourism; plateaus give minerals; plains give food crops
Thar Desert: camels, saving rainwater, loose light clothes
traps: Plains are low and flat; raised flat land is a plateau
Don't say plains are known for minerals; plateaus are
Desert life uses camels, not yaks
